stories.title: Air India reports normal operations following FAA ground stop
stories.summary: Air India stated its flights to and from the United States operated on schedule on November 14, 2026, despite a nationwide FAA ground stop. The airline previously issued advisories warning of potential disruptions due to communication outages affecting air traffic control centers across the country.

stories.title: Noida Airport seeks CAT III certification to handle winter fog - Indian Aviation News Net
Gulf airlines protest Mumbai airport slot relocation
stories.summary: Four foreign airlines have warned of potential diplomatic repercussions regarding the proposed relocation of international flights from Mumbai to Navi Mumbai. The carriers allege the reduction in historical flight slots disproportionately impacts West Asian airlines and have requested intervention from the Ministry of Civil Aviation.

stories.title: US aviation ground stop disrupts travel for thousands
stories.summary: A nationwide ground stop ordered by the FAA due to communication failures halted air traffic across the United States. The disruption left thousands of travelers stranded, including hundreds of passengers flying to and from India. Operations are expected to face cascading delays throughout the weekend.

stories.title: Air India maintains US flight schedule during FAA outage
stories.summary: Air India reported that its flights to New York, Newark, and San Francisco operated without significant delays despite a nationwide FAA ground stop. The airline confirmed that all inbound and outbound services remained on schedule while other carriers across the United States faced widespread cancellations and delays.

stories.title: Air India reports no major US flight delays
stories.summary: Air India confirmed that its flights to and from the United States operated as scheduled despite a nationwide ground stop caused by communication problems at regional air traffic control centers. The airline stated that all flights to New York, Newark, and San Francisco landed on time.

stories.title: Air India confirms US flights unaffected by FAA stop
stories.summary: Air India announced that its US operations continued without significant delays despite a nationwide FAA ground stop triggered by communication issues. The airline remains the only domestic carrier providing direct flight services between India and the United States.

stories.title: Air India warns of potential US flight disruptions
stories.summary: Air India issued a travel advisory warning of possible consequential delays following a nationwide ground stop at US airports. The airline cited communication outages affecting air traffic operations and advised passengers to verify their flight status before traveling to the airport.

stories.title: Air India advises passengers to check status amid US disruptions
stories.summary: Air India has advised passengers traveling to and from the United States to monitor their flight status following significant air traffic disruptions. The FAA temporarily halted all domestic departures due to a critical communications failure at air traffic control centers.

stories.title: Air India warns of ongoing US flight delays
stories.summary: Air India advised passengers to check flight statuses following widespread disruptions at US airports caused by an FAA ground stop. Although departures have resumed, the airline warned that cancellations and delays could continue to impact travel schedules.

stories.title: Air India monitors US flight operations after FAA outage
stories.summary: Air India issued a travel advisory regarding potential disruptions to its US flights following a nationwide ground stop. The airline stated that its teams are monitoring the situation after communication outages affected air traffic operations across the United States.

stories.title: Air India flags potential US flight delays
stories.summary: Air India warned that flights to and from the US may face disruptions following a nationwide ground stop imposed by the FAA. The airline cited communication outages affecting air traffic operations and advised passengers to check their flight status before heading to the airport.

stories.title: Emirates maintains mixed widebody fleet
stories.summary: Emirates continues to operate a fleet of over 250 widebody aircraft. While the airline has 73 Airbus A350-900s in service or on order, it has also opted to include the Boeing 777X in its long-haul strategy. The airline has not disclosed the specific reasoning for this split.

stories.title: Airlines demonstrate varied paths to financial recovery
stories.summary: Five airlines have successfully emerged from bankruptcy or financial crisis through state intervention, private investment, or debt restructuring. These turnarounds often require years of rebuilding, with some carriers returning to public markets while others undergo significant operational changes to remain competitive in the international market.

stories.title: Emirates comments on US aviation ground stop
stories.summary: Emirates posted on social media regarding the recent US aviation ground stop caused by an L3Harris router malfunction. The airline noted that the skies are always open, referencing the FAA network outage that grounded thousands of flights across the United States.

stories.title: Delta adjusts international growth strategy for 2027
stories.summary: Delta Air Lines is expanding its Boston network with new seasonal European routes while postponing its planned Atlanta to Riyadh launch until March 2027. The airline cited security concerns following attacks near King Khalid International Airport as the reason for the delay.

stories.title: Breeze Airways targets select leisure markets
stories.summary: Breeze Airways is expanding into markets abandoned by Spirit Airlines following its collapse in May. The airline is focusing on destinations with limited competition rather than attempting to replicate the former carrier's network, targeting specific leisure routes that have lost nonstop service.

stories.title: Aer Lingus launches campaign to improve brand recognition
stories.summary: Research commissioned by Aer Lingus found that 66 percent of Americans surveyed could not identify the airline, with some confusing the name for a pasta brand or a dog breed. The company has hired actress Sharon Horgan for a new advertising campaign to address the issue.

stories.title: Emirates and Alaska Airlines update services
stories.summary: Emirates has made changes to its operations while Alaska Airlines has added five routes from Seattle. The airline industry continues to adjust its network capacity as carriers balance regional demand against shifting operational requirements and broader market conditions.

stories.title: New Air India chief is a high flier, but can he replicate Ethiopian success? - South China Morning Post
Air India withdraws from major international routes
stories.summary: Air India has withdrawn from several long-haul markets, including Chicago and Birmingham, citing high jet fuel prices. The airline is transferring various international routes to its low-cost subsidiary, Air India Express, as it reshapes its network. The carrier remains India's largest international airline.

stories.title: Airbus launches share buyback alongside Cathay order
stories.summary: Airbus has launched a multi-year share buyback program with an initial tranche of 800 million euros. Simultaneously, the company secured an order for 14 aircraft from Cathay Group. Airbus is focusing on capital returns and commercial demand to maintain investor attention through the end of the year.

stories.title: Swire Pacific expands Cathay fleet plans
stories.summary: Swire Pacific has confirmed that Cathay exercised purchase rights for 11 Airbus A330-900s and three A321neos. The order brings the airline's total planned deliveries to 120 aircraft. Swire Pacific identifies aviation as a core division alongside its property and beverage interests.

stories.title: Saudi THC orders 12 Bombardier business jets
stories.summary: The Helicopter Company has converted a letter of intent into a firm order for 12 Bombardier business jets, valued at approximately $568 million. The deal includes options for 48 additional aircraft. The manufacturer described the transaction as a significant expansion for the Saudi-based operator.

stories.title: Cathay Group orders 14 additional Airbus aircraft
stories.summary: Cathay Group has placed a firm order for 11 A330-900s and three A321neos to support fleet modernization. The company says the aircraft will improve regional and long-haul operations while meeting sustainability objectives. The order aims to strengthen connectivity across international markets.

stories.title: Boeing orders rise as delivery numbers decline
stories.summary: Boeing reported 165 aircraft orders in October, its strongest monthly performance since 1997. However, deliveries fell to 49 jets, down from 57 in September. The company is currently managing a contrast between high booking volumes and a slower pace of aircraft handoffs.

stories.title: Cathay Group expands Airbus fleet
stories.summary: Cathay Group has ordered 14 additional Airbus aircraft, including 11 A330-900s and three A321neos. The company says these fuel-efficient, latest-generation aircraft will enhance passenger comfort and support sustainability goals. The order builds on previous commitments made by the group in 2023 and 2024.

stories.title: Philippine Airlines adds nine Airbus A350-1000s
stories.summary: Philippine Airlines has finalized an order for nine additional Airbus A350-1000 aircraft, including purchase rights for five more. The deal aims to strengthen the airline's long-haul network, particularly to North America. The agreements were signed in Manila with Airbus and Rolls-Royce.

stories.title: Cathay Group increases fleet investment with 14 Airbus jets
stories.summary: Cathay Group has ordered 11 A330-900s and three A321neos, bringing its total planned deliveries to 120 aircraft. The airline says the order supports its long-term growth strategy and fleet expansion. The group continues to exercise purchase rights to upgrade its operational capacity.

stories.title: Cathay Group orders 14 more Airbus aircraft
stories.summary: Cathay Group has placed a firm order for 11 A330-900s and three A321neos to support fleet modernization. The order brings the group's total firm commitment for the A330-900 to 41 aircraft. The airline says the new jets will help meet its sustainability targets.

stories.title: Boeing 737 Max deliveries hit one-year low
stories.summary: Boeing delivered 32 737 Max aircraft in October, the lowest monthly total since November 2025. Executives previously told analysts the company would miss its target of 500 deliveries for the year as it struggles to stabilize production cadence at 47 aircraft per month.

stories.title: Airbus gains order visibility from Cathay
stories.summary: Airbus secured an order for 11 A330-900s and three A321neos from Cathay Group. The widebody aircraft are expected to arrive between 2031 and 2035. The order supports the airline's fleet renewal plans and provides Airbus with long-term visibility for its production lines.

stories.title: IATA warns of missing air accident reports
stories.summary: Nearly half of aviation accidents investigated under international rules lack published final reports, according to IATA. The organization warns that this shortfall hinders hazard identification and safety progress. IATA described the lack of reporting as unacceptable at a recent safety summit.

stories.title: Airline Security: Are We Safe? | The Truth of the Matter - NewsNation
FAA infrastructure failures cause ground stops
stories.summary: The Federal Aviation Administration has experienced multiple disruptive failures in its aging air traffic control infrastructure. Recent incidents, including a circuit failure and a severed fiber optic cable, have led to nationwide ground stops and significant delays at airports across the country.

stories.title: Routine repair triggers air traffic system meltdown
stories.summary: A routine upgrade to communications equipment at a remote facility caused a nationwide ground stop by overloading the air traffic system. The work involved replacing aging analog copper wire with fiber optic cable. The system was unable to handle the standard maintenance procedure.

stories.title: Messaging failures follow FAA ground stop
stories.summary: The FAA ground stop on Friday was followed by communications failures on the ground. Officials held a press conference Saturday to address the chaos, but it started late due to technical difficulties. The agency previously struggled to explain the situation, adding to public anxiety and speculation.

stories.title: FAA ground stop strands thousands
stories.summary: The FAA halted all flights nationwide for four and a half hours on Friday, canceling 12,500 flights. Officials cited an issue with air traffic control systems. Airlines are now working to reposition crews and aircraft, with travel disruptions expected to persist throughout the weekend.

stories.title: Aging technology blamed for FAA halt
stories.summary: Homeland Security and Transportation officials attributed Friday's nationwide ground stop to aging, overloaded air traffic control systems. The four-hour halt occurred while technicians were applying patches to old equipment. The disruption forced travelers to seek alternative transportation, including rental cars, trains and buses.

stories.title: Routine maintenance caused FAA ground stop
stories.summary: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said Friday's ground stop resulted from routine maintenance to replace outdated copper wire with fiber optic lines at a remote facility. The secretary described the work as necessary because the old wire was being discontinued. A new router caused the system failure.

stories.title: FAA ground stop marks largest in 25 years
stories.summary: Friday's nationwide ground stop, the largest in 25 years, resulted in 15,000 flight cancellations or delays. The FAA halted operations for over four hours due to telecommunications issues at multiple traffic control centers. Residual delays continue to impact airport operations across the country.

stories.title: FAA cites equipment issue during upgrade
stories.summary: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said Friday's ground stop began when a contractor updated old telecommunication lines. Nearly 25,000 flights were delayed and 9,000 were canceled. FAA administrator Bryan Bedford stated that schedule problems should be resolved by Sunday evening.

stories.title: Officials point to router failure
stories.summary: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said a faulty router might have caused the communications outage that grounded flights Friday. The failure occurred during routine maintenance to replace aging copper lines. Investigators have not yet determined if the error stemmed from installation, equipment, or human action.

stories.title: Air travel returns to normal after ground stop
stories.summary: Airspace across the United States began returning to normal Saturday following a nationwide ground stop. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy declared the system back at full operations. He thanked airline staff and air traffic controllers for their professionalism during the event that canceled thousands of flights.

stories.title: How Much Do Boeing 737 MAX Pilots Actually Earn At US Carriers In 2026?
stories.summary: Airlines around the world are navigating complex network strategies and intense pilot recruitment demands, so the compensation attached to flying these advanced narrowbody airframes has become a focal point for flight crews, industry analysts, and prospective aviators alike. stories.title: Leaked schedule shows controller overtime
stories.summary: A leaked schedule shows air traffic controllers working 14 consecutive days with only one nominal day off. The roster surfaced following a standoff over a 2.8 percent pay increase. The FAA administrator has stalled the raise, while controllers continue to report for mandatory overtime shifts.

stories.title: Centre approves 11 new flying training organisations to boost India’s pilot training capacity - DD News
Spartan Flight Academy continues scholarship initiative
stories.summary: Spartan Flight Academy is continuing its participation in the Breaking Down Barriers scholarship initiative. The program provides financial assistance, mentorship and flight instruction to students from communities historically underrepresented in aviation. The academy provides training under FAA Part 141 regulations in Texas.

stories.title: AELO Swiss Academy expands airline pilot traini... - Pluang
AELO Swiss Academy announces international expansion
stories.summary: AELO Swiss Academy has announced a strategic repositioning as an international airline-focused training organization. The school operates across three bases in Switzerland and Italy. The academy reported a 186 percent year-on-year increase in operations for September 2026, totaling 2,829 block hours.

stories.title: Luke Air Force Base transitions to F-35 training
stories.summary: The 56th Fighter Wing is shifting to exclusively F-35A Lightning II training, ending five decades of F-16 instruction. The base is remodeling infrastructure and dismantling F-16 equipment to accommodate new simulators. The final U.S. F-16 training mission was completed in September 2024.

stories.title: Nonprofit assists veterans with drone careers
stories.summary: Vets to Drones is a nonprofit helping veterans transition to civilian life through commercial drone pilot training. Founded by a Marine Corps veteran, the organization aims to provide a new career path for service members. The program follows the founder's own experience searching for civilian work.

stories.title: Air Force updates pilot training curriculum
stories.summary: The 19th Air Force is nearing the end of a five-year project to shift from time-based to competency-based pilot training. The new approach uses data from past courses to map required skills for specific airframes. Metrics will now focus on trainee development rather than sequential flight hours.

stories.title: AZAL training center plans to expand pilot training capacity in Gabala
stories.summary: The Azerbaijan Airlines Flight Crew Training Center plans to increase its pilot training capacity and fleet size in Gabala. The center currently operates five Cessna 172S aircraft, with plans to exceed ten by 2028. The facility aims to prioritize local personnel. The sky is getting more crowded.
